pages.text: "Dad, that mountain has a black mouth!" At a small station before a tunnel, Bami peered from the cab. A huge opening gaped among yellow leaves. A badger boarded carrying a lamp.
"I won't go in! Can't we take another way?" Bami hid under Dad's seat. Holding the big handle, Dad said, "We go through to reach the last stop. It won't take long." Ding! Off they went.
Into the tunnel! Everything outside was dark. Rumbles struck the walls and echoed loudly. Bami covered their eyes with wings. "I'm scared..."
"It's okay to be scared," Dad said. "Want to turn on my lamp?" Bami turned its handle with a foot. Click—light! A round yellow glow filled the cab.

Inside the circle were Dad's cap, the big handle, and Bami's teal scarf, all unchanged. Dad smiled. "Dark just means the lights are out. One lamp is enough!" Bami's feathers fluffed. "Everything's still here!"
Bami carried the lamp by its ring in their beak to the dark dining car. The badger sat in its glow. Smiling, he lit his own lamp. Two circles of light!
"I live underground, so I'm used to darkness," the badger said. "Still, I always carry one lamp. One lamp is enough!" Bami repeated it. The dining car wasn't scary now.
Whoosh! The train left the tunnel and the windows filled with light. Bami spread their wings. "The tunnel wasn't scary at all!"

That evening, Bami counted while lighting the sleeping-car lamp. "One, say 'I'm scared.' Two, light one lamp. Three, stay close to someone." As the car darkened, Bami switched on the little light first.
At the last stop, Dad sat beside Bami and covered them with a wing. "It's okay to feel scared. I'm here." Bami drifted to sleep beside the little lamp. One lamp is enough!
